steps.title: Two ways to tell it
paragraphs: Version 1: The dog went across the yard. It was very fast. It got the ball.
Version 2: The dog rocketed across the yard, ears flapping, and snatched the ball mid-bounce.
Same dog. Same yard. Which one can you picture?

cards.title: Weak verbs vs. strong verbs
cards.body: Weak verbs like went, got, said and looked tell us very little. Strong verbs like stumbled, grabbed, whispered and glared paint a picture.

cards.title: Cut the "very"
cards.note: Swap "very + word" for one stronger word: very tired → exhausted, very happy → thrilled, very cold → freezing.

cards.title: Precise nouns
cards.text: Not "a bird" but "a crow". Not "a car" but "a rusty pickup truck". Not "food" but "cold pizza".
cards.note: The more precise the word, the clearer the picture.

cards.title: Spot the strong verbs
cards.text: Mateo sprinted to the door, yanked it open, and gasped.

prompts: Which weak word did you replace with the best strong word? Write both.
Pick one new strong verb you want to use again. Use it in a sentence.
